text:
alex: quick syncwe're seeing cross-region attribution arrive 5-20m late and compact ledger drops partials.
priya: customer reported missing tokens on invoice. we need non-destructive repairs.
jonah: two options: keep state longer (hold GC) or emit idempotent repair events. holding GC increases memory and latency.
mei: prefer repair events + idempotency. need canonical keys: fingerprint+epoch+source_priority.
alex: draft schema idea: type=repair, fingerprint, epoch, delta, reason. put in event stream flagged as repair.
priya: ordering concern  what if final attribution arrives right after repair? avoid flip-flops.
jonah: rule: first non-repair final wins. repairs apply only if no final exists or if row marked partial. repair noop if final exists.
mei: fallback: background scan of raw events up to 7d to rebuild rows if repair missed. cheaper memory, more IO.
alex: proposed defaults: 30m grace, repairs on ingest, scan fallback to 7d, tenant-configurable grace for enterprise.
priya: metrics: repair_emitted, repair_applied, repair_noop, scan_rebuilt_rows. alerts if repair_applied rate spikes per-tenant.
jonah: audit requirement: every repair writes audit record (from,to,actor,timestamp) for disputes.
mei: security: require signed repair events (HMAC) from regional gateways. ops-bot: "repair pipeline now requires hmac header (deployed) :white_check_mark:"
alex: owners: jonah RFC for state machine + upsert semantics, mei observability tests, priya tenant API. small integration simulating 3-region lateness.
jonah: will draft RFC and include example upsert pseudo-sql for merge rules.
priya: runbook note: if repair_applied > 0.1% billed tokens, pause GC for tenant and run integrity scan, escalate to SE.
mei: adding unit tests for merge rules and replay simulation.
alex: thanks all, close thread.
